articles.t: Walmart GTA 6 Preorders Will Get a 'Surprise and Delight' Bag, It's Claimed
articles.chapeau: It has been reported on social media that users picking up GTA 6 pre-orders at Walmart will receive an exclusive goodie bag.
articles.txt:
It has been suggested on social media that ‘select Walmart stores’ will be running a limited promotion to celebrate the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. Customers who pre-order GTA 6 online with Walmart and collect in-store will receive a ‘surprise and delight’ bag upon collection, but what’s in that bag hasn’t been revealed.
It’s hardly a reach to assume that one of the biggest retailers in the world will have scored some kind of special merchandise run with Rockstar Games to promote and honor the launch of GTA 6, of course.
In a post on social media, it was claimed that Rockstar Games has joined forces with Walmart to offer ‘surprise and delight’ bags to select customers who pre-order their copy of Grand Theft Auto 6 online with the retailer.
EXCLUSIVE: Rockstar Games is partnering with Walmart to do an online pre-order promotion. Each online pre-order will receive a “surprise and delight bag” within the package. It’s unknown what the mystery bonus will be at the moment. [via @nxrcssist ] pic.twitter.com/npGnwApOuo
The mysterious packages will be available from November 12th, which is when customers can pick up their copy of the game. That’s when GTA 6’s pre-load window opens up, and just because you can get your copy of the game from Walmart (and other retailers) doesn’t mean you can play it then.
After all, you’re picking up a code in a box. The game won’t go live until November 19th.
As for what’s in the surprise and delight package from Walmart, it could be almost anything. It could be a poster, an in-game map, a badge or a button, a keychain, or one of dozens of knick-knacks created to celebrate the launch.
I’ve pinged Walmart to see if I can learn more in the meantime.

News News Tripping Animals' GTA 6 Beers Resell for Over $200 on eBay Bringing a new definition to "beer money" News By RC Staff
Key Points Tripping Animals confirmed Friday that its Pißwasser, Patriot, and No Mames Vice City beers are on sale in Miami
Three-can sets are reselling for $150 to $200 on eBay, with single Patriot and Pißwasser cans topping $40
The beers are sold only at the Doral taproom and select Miami stores, with no online sales of any kind
If you’ve ever dreamed of cracking open an ice cold Pißwasser after a day spent road raging and shooting people in the face, Rockstar is making it a reality. Tripping Animals Brewing pulled the trigger on its GTA beer lineup this week, and fans who can’t get to South Florida immediately started paying triple digit prices for cans that cost about as much as any other craft beer. The best part is you don’t even have to sell the beer. Drink it, keep the can, and flip the empty. This is the most literal definition of beer money we’ve ever covered.
We first flagged these beers in October, when GTA 6 beer labels turned up in the federal Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau database. The approvals landed between late September and mid-October, and while neither Rockstar nor the brewery said anything publicly, nobody gets federal label approval for a beer they don’t plan to pour.
On Friday, Tripping Animals confirmed the beers were available at its Doral taproom and “at select locations around Miami.” There’s no online store, no shipping, and no preorder. If you want one, you have to go find it.
The lineup has three cans. Pißwasser and Patriot are real world recreations of beers that have appeared across the GTA series, and a Patriot six-pack even showed up in a GTA 6 trailer. Both are 4.2% ABV lagers. No Mames Vice City is a GTA spin on the brewery’s own 6% ABV No Mames lager. It’s one more piece of Rockstar’s campaign to turn Miami into Vice City ahead of the November 19 launch.
eBay has exploded with listings. Sets of all three cans are reselling for $150 to $200, while single Patriot and Pißwasser cans are moving for $40 or more . Some sellers have bundled the cans with limited edition bottle openers and napkins sold at Tripping Animals’ taphouse, and these listings have climbed to over $400.
eBay prohibits alcohol sales, so everything moving there is empty cans. After eBay’s 13.6% fees, a $175 three-can set nets about $151 before shipping, and a $40 single nets about $35. Subtract the cost of the beer you drank anyway, and the margins are absurd.
Patriot and Pißwasser lead on singles, which makes sense. Those names carry nearly two decades of franchise nostalgia, while No Mames Vice City is essentially a reskin of an existing Tripping Animals beer. It still matters for completing the set.
GTA has one of the biggest fanbases in gaming, and the beer is limited to one metro area with zero online sales. Tripping Animals hosts a beer finder for its retailers, but it won’t confirm whether a store has the GTA cans in stock, so even locals have to hunt. GTA fans have also proven they’ll pay for oddities: used Burger Shot wrappers from the Kaseya Center sold for $80 or more .
If you’re in the Miami area, there’s no reason to drink any other beer right now. You need to be 21 to buy (obviously), and only empties can go on eBay. Rinse and dry them completely, avoid dents, and ship in a box.
In other GTA 6 news, Travis Scott’s upcoming collab with Rockstar and Nike for a limited edition Air Force 1 collection has leaked online . Pairs are expected to go on sale November 19 alongside GTA 6.

articles.chapeau: Rockstar's next big GTA 6 promotion is a three-way collab with Travis Scott and Nike for a line of limited edition Air Force 1 Lows
articles.txt:

News News Travis Scott's GTA 6 AF1 Sneakers Drop November 19 Talk about star power News By RC Staff
Key Points All three Travis Scott x Rockstar Games x Nike Air Force 1 Lows will retail for $130 each
The pack releases November 19 through Nike and select retailers, the same day GTA 6 launches
Travis Scott’s last Air Force 1, the Ice Blue, retailed for $120 and has sold for over $550 on StockX
Rockstar has spent the last few months turning Miami into one giant GTA 6 billboard, and now its marketing machine has pulled in one of the few names in sneakers that can match its hype. Travis Scott, Nike, and Rockstar Games are dropping a three-pair Air Force 1 pack timed to the biggest game launch in years, and the first leaked images already have collectors circling the date. Scott’s AF1s have a long track record of selling for multiples of retail, and anything with a GTA 6 logo on it has been flying off shelves since summer. Put the two together and this is shaping up to be one of the hottest sneaker drops of the year.
The collab surfaced over the weekend when Sole Retriever reported the pack , which added two pairs labeled “Nike x Cactus Jack x RS” to its release calendar, and leaker Sneaker Market RO, who confirmed a third. Nothing has been officially announced by Nike, Rockstar, or Scott yet.
Only the black pair has been seen so far, and it’s a good one. The upper is all black with Scott’s signature reverse Swoosh and a debossed pattern that may trace Vice City’s street layout. A pink and white GTA 6 money band wraps the toebox, and six stars on the medial side and in pink on the outsole nod to the game’s max wanted level. Expect the other two pairs to follow a similar design language.
Scott’s ties to the game go beyond footwear. His track “Rhyno” is part of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album, and Sole Retriever reports he’s also part of a four-way apparel collab with Rockstar, Nike, and the Miami Heat. That one likely ties into the Heat’s Night in Vice City game on November 18 , the night before GTA 6 hits consoles.
This is about as strong a setup as sneakers get. Travis Scott collabs move on their own, and the GTA 6 crowd has shown it will pay up for almost anything Rockstar touches. Even the Burger Shot trash bags from the Kaseya Center have been reselling for up to $80 . Plenty of collectors will want all three pairs, which adds demand on top of the usual Travis and Nike buyers.
The closest comp is Scott’s Ice Blue Air Force 1 , which dropped in September through a NYC pop-up and his website with no broad release. That pair has sold for over four times retail on StockX. Expect lower numbers here. Nike and select retailers is a much wider channel, and three colorways splits demand. There are no sold comps yet, so treat any projection as an estimate. If the black pair lands around $300 on StockX, you’d net roughly $264 after a 12% fee, about double what you paid before tax and shipping.
StockX is the move for these, with GOAT as a backup. Nike typically accepts returns on unworn pairs bought directly, but check terms at checkout since policies at select retailers vary and some collab launches are final sale.
Full details should land soon. Rockstar has revealed something new every Thursday since the Extended Look trailer aired in August, and we’d expect that pattern to hold through launch. Keep an eye on Rockstar, Nike, and Travis Scott’s socials this week, especially Thursday, November 5, and be ready for the official reveal and release method. We’ll update this article as soon as it drops.

articles.t: GTA 6, Nike et Travis Scott prépareraient trois baskets
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 pourrait accueillir trois Nike Air Force 1 conçues avec Travis Scott et Rockstar Games. Une sortie le 19 novembre à 130 dollars est évoquée.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 GTA 6, une collaboration entre Nike, Travis Scott et Rockstar Games se prépare pour le 19 novembre Florian Prache Publié le 01 Novembre 2026 à 22h44 3 minutes de lecture Ajoutez-nous à vos sources sur Google Sommaire GTA 6 pourrait avoir droit à trois Nike Air Force 1 exclusives Des détails inspirés de GTA 6, mais un design qui divise déjà Travis Scott participe déjà à l'univers musical de GTA 6 Résumer l'article Résumé rapide de l'article
Alors que GTA 6 sortira le 19 novembre 2026 , une collaboration inattendue fait parler d'elle dans le monde des sneakers. Selon plusieurs informations relayées par des médias spécialisés, Rockstar Games, Nike et Travis Scott prépareraient une collection de trois paires de Nike Air Force 1 Low aux couleurs de Grand Theft Auto VI via prm.stocks.01 . Une sortie serait prévue le même jour que le jeu, avec un prix annoncé de 130 dollars par paire. Attention toutefois, aucune annonce officielle n'a encore été faite.
La sortie de GTA 6 pourrait être accompagnée d'une collaboration avec deux grands noms de la mode et de la musique. D'après les informations initialement partagées par Sneaker Market Romania , puis relayées par Sneaker News et Sole Retriever, trois modèles de Nike Air Force 1 Low '07 seraient actuellement en préparation.
Cette collection réunirait Rockstar Games, Nike et Cactus Jack, la marque du rappeur Travis Scott.
Selon les premières informations, les trois paires seraient commercialisées le 19 novembre 2026 , pour un prix de 130 dollars chacune aux États-Unis. Aucun tarif en euros ni aucune disponibilité française n'ont encore été confirmés.
Des visuels présentés comme ceux de la version noire commencent à circuler sur Internet. Ils montrent une Nike Air Force 1 au design relativement sobre, avec plusieurs éléments faisant référence à l'univers de Grand Theft Auto.
Parmi les détails évoqués, on retrouve notamment six étoiles roses rappelant l'indice de recherche maximal de GTA , ainsi qu'une bande décorative imitant une liasse de billets sur l'avant de la chaussure.
Le modèle disposerait également de lacets interchangeables, dont une version rose particulièrement visible, et d'un emballage spécifique à cette collaboration.
Cependant, ces visuels n'ont pas été authentifiés par Nike ou Rockstar Games . Il faut donc rester prudent concernant l'apparence définitive de la collection.
Les premières réactions partagées autour de ces images sont d'ailleurs mitigées. Certains trouvent la version noire trop classique pour une collaboration associant trois noms aussi importants. Le manque de couleurs et de références visuelles immédiatement reconnaissables à GTA 6 semble notamment décevoir une partie des internautes.
Si cette collaboration vestimentaire reste une rumeur, les liens entre Travis Scott et Grand Theft Auto VI sont, eux, bien réels.
Rockstar Games a officiellement annoncé la participation de l'artiste à la bande originale du jeu avec le morceau RHYNO, produit par Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, ancien membre de Daft Punk.
Cette chanson fait partie de Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , un projet comprenant 34 titres originaux, dont la sortie est également fixée au 19 novembre.
Une collection de sneakers viendrait donc prolonger cette collaboration musicale, tout en accompagnant le lancement du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games.
Pour le moment, aucune confirmation officielle n'a été publiée concernant les Nike Air Force 1 GTA 6. La date du 19 novembre et le prix de 130 dollars proviennent d'informations issues du secteur des sneakers et doivent encore être confirmés par les marques concernées.
Si cette collaboration se concrétise, les prochaines annonces permettront de découvrir les véritables modèles, leurs tarifs européens et les modalités d'achat en France.

articles.t: GTA 6 pourrait vous faire économiser plus de 4 000 euros : l
articles.chapeau: Un millionnaire britannique affirme que GTA 6 peut alléger votre budget de plus de 4 000 €. Nous avons confronté son calcul viral aux chiffres français.
articles.txt:
Un millionnaire britannique affirme que GTA 6 peut alléger votre budget de plus de 4 000 €. Nous avons confronté son calcul viral aux chiffres français.
Un millionnaire britannique affirme que GTA 6 pourrait vous faire gagner de l’argent. Dans une vidéo virale intitulée « How GTA 6 Could Save You $5,000 » (soit environ 4 600 €), le créateur finance Mark Tilbury entre dans un magasin, attrape une boîte du jeu et explique, calculette en main, comment un titre vendu plein tarif pourrait alléger votre budget sorties.
Le clip, repéré par Insider Gaming et le journaliste Grant Taylor-Hill , fait évidemment réagir dans un contexte de hausse des prix des jeux AAA. Avec une sortie fixée au 19 novembre 2026 sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X|S , Grand Theft Auto VI sera-t-il vraiment un bon plan financier ou juste un joli storytelling marketing ?
Le raisonnement de Mark Tilbury est simple. Il part d’un prix de 99,99 $ (environ 95 €) pour GTA 6, estime la campagne à 80 heures , soit environ 1,24 $ l’heure de divertissement. En ajoutant quêtes annexes et exploration de l’État fictif de Leonida, il affirme descendre « as little as 50 cents per hour ».
Derrière, Tilbury enchaîne : quatre heures de jeu chaque soir pendant 50 nuits, c’est 200 heures passées à Vice City . Si vous remplaciez ces sessions par des sorties à 100 $ (environ 90 €) la soirée entre restaurants, bars et activités, l’addition atteindrait 5 000 $ (près de 4 600 €). Sur le papier, vous « économisez » donc plus de 4 000 €.
Côté français, le tarif officiel est de 79,99 € pour l’ édition Standard et 99,99 € pour l’édition Ultimate, mais certaines enseignes comme E.Leclerc, Amazon ou Auchan proposent déjà la boîte autour de 60 €. À ce prix, jouer 100 heures ramène le coût à 0,60 € l’heure, 200 heures à seulement 0,30 €.
En face, une soirée classique dans une grande ville peut vite dépasser les 80 à 100 € par personne : environ 30 € pour un restaurant milieu de gamme, 25 à 35 € de cocktails, plus transports et éventuellement cinéma. L’ordre de grandeur utilisé par Tilbury tient donc la route, mais correspond clairement à un style de vie très festif.
Reste la vraie question : auriez-vous vraiment dépensé ces 5 000 $ (environ 4 600 €) sans acheter GTA 6 ? Pour beaucoup, le jeu remplacera surtout d’autres activités sur écran, pas cinquante restos-bars. Tilbury oublie aussi des coûts bien réels : console PS5 ou Xbox Series X|S , abonnement en ligne, achats in-game. Oui, le coût par heure est bas si vous jouez beaucoup, mais l’ »économie » de plus de 4 000 € sert surtout d’argument choc pour vous garder à Vice City.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' file size reportedly revealed and it's gargantuan
articles.chapeau: That's no surprise.
articles.txt:
You might need to take a break from salivating over every Grand Theft Auto VI trailer to clear some space on your PS5 or Xbox hard drive.
An X account called PlayStation Game Size allegedly caught wind of the install size for GTA 6 and posted it on Tuesday. Ladies and gentlemen, wait for the reveal...it's apparently 210GB. That's pretty huge (though still not as big as Call of Duty ), which should be a surprise to no one. However, given that a base PS5 has a little less than 1TB of usable storage space, you might need to do some virtual inventory management if you also keep other big games installed.
A 210GB file size for a purely single-player (for now) game is massive. Just to compare it to a couple of other major open-world games from this console generation, Elden Ring is only about 65GB, Assassin's Creed Shadows was just north of 100GB, and Marvel's Spider-Man 2 asked for 98GB of space on your hard drive. That doesn't necessarily mean GTA 6 is twice as big as those games, as a lot of different variables can factor into file size, but it does mean that it's probably pretty huge regardless of how it compares to anything else.
Only a few more weeks now until it's finally in our hands. Remember: GTA 6 officially launched Nov. 19.

articles.t: Grand Theft Auto 6 Download Size Revealed To Be 210 GB
articles.chapeau: Grand Theft Auto 6's install size will come in at a whopping 210 GB, it has been revealed, making it one of the largest games ever.
articles.txt:
In a post on social media, user PlayStation Game Size revealed that the complete download size of the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 will be a whopping 210 GB. Insider Gaming can corroborate this information.
This makes Grand Theft Auto 6 one of the largest games ever made , by base file size. It’s about what everyone was expecting, but it’s sure to clog up networks worldwide when preloading starts on November 12.
We all knew GTA 6 would be a big game . The screenshots and videos we’ve seen thus far have portrayed a gargantuan open world packed to the brim with activities and side content, along with what could be the densest story the franchise has ever seen.
In a recent post on social media, PlayStation Game Size, a popular datamining profile, revealed the install size for GTA 6 at the time of writing :
🚨 Grand Theft Auto VI – 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝 𝐒𝐢𝐳𝐞 : 210 GB – 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 ($79.99) Pre-Load : November 12 Release : November 19 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 : Midnight pic.twitter.com/5vXkgnqfC7
I say at the time of writing because things are always subject to change. Until it’s safely installed on your console, things could shift, and assuming there’s a day-one patch, even when the clock strikes midnight, you might be left downloading something additional.
In the recent GTA 6 space, we saw the actor rumored to be playing Lucia Caminos, Manni Perez, appearing on a livestream and tactfully dodging questions about the upcoming game. However, she was offering some coy glances to the camera that set social media ablaze with claims that she was surreptitiously confirming what everyone believes.

articles.t: OnlyFans star blasts girlfriends banning boyfriends from GTA VI : ‘At least he’s not cheating in real life’
articles.chapeau: Is it cheating if it’s in a video game? An OnlyFans star says women are being too strict on boyfriends.
articles.txt:
Is it cheating if it’s in a video game? An OnlyFans star says women are being too strict on boyfriends.
With the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI on Nov. 19, millionaire OnlyFans creator Skylar Mae is weighing in on whether virtual infidelity counts as real cheating — and she’s urging women to relax and let their partners enjoy the game.
The hit action-adventure video game franchise has long drawn scrutiny for its explicit content, since the first edition was released in 1997, for its simulated strip clubs with lap dances and optional prostitution gameplay.
While some partners express concern over the game’s steamy features , Mae argues women should care more about real-life loyalty than pixels on a screen.
OnlyFans creator Skylar Mae speaks about the debate over whether playing Grand Theft Auto VI is considered cheating. Rockstar Games “They could be out at a real strip club or actually cheating on you in real life,” Mae told Jam Press. “It’s the same thing with OnlyFans. Hey, at least they’re doing it at home and not physically cheating on you with someone else!”
The game has sparked fierce debate across social media, with gamers and their partners disputing over whether building virtual relationships or visiting in-game strip clubs crosses the line into emotional infidelity.
Mae said she has heard girls say they don’t let their boyfriends play GTA because they are maintaining a relationship with the other main character, which she said she finds comical, and said it’s the same thing as them having an OnlyFans subscription.
Mae says she doesn’t understand why women are “getting so worked up” over a fictional relationship.
Her stance comes in response to a wave of TikTok videos featuring women declaring that their boyfriends are banned from playing GTA VI because of its lead characters, Jason and Lucia.
Shelby Haas, who boasts 1.1 million followers on TikTok, posted a viral video stating her fiancé isn’t allowed to play GTA VI after learning players must maintain a relationship with a female character, text her, take her on dates, and engage in virtual intimacy. She added that she also disapproves of the game’s strip clubs and nudist themes.
“Don’t let your boyfriend, fiancé or husband play GTA6,” she ranted to viewers. “The entire male population is going way downhill… why are you in love with pixels?”
The clip ignited sharp debate. Some commenters agreed with Haas, calling the gameplay “seriously weird” and arguing that “if there was an equally popular game for girls, these men would flip out.”
But others say women being “insecure about a video game” is more of a reflection on their insecurities.
OnlyFans creator Skylar Mae speaks about the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, arguing women should let their partners enjoy the game. Instagram/Skyler Mae “It’s just a game… Are we that insecure???” commented one user on her video.
“If you are worried about a fictional character… that’s a reflection on you,” wrote another.
Mae agrees with the critics of the ban, believing women should appreciate having partners who prefer gaming over real-world trouble. Rather than banning the game, she suggests women pick up a controller themselves.
“My advice is to 100% play the game for yourself!” she said. “I think these girls should just jump on the game, take a look and chill out, because at least their boyfriends aren’t cheating on them in real life!”

GTA 6 x Travis Scott x Nike : Trois Air Force 1 débarquent le jour de la sortie du jeu 01-11-2026 20:25 DL GAMING
Une collaboration entre Rockstar Games, Nike et Travis Scott se prépare-t-elle pour accompagner le lancement de Grand Theft Auto VI ? Selon plusieurs informations relayées dans la sphère sneakers, trois nouvelles Nike Air Force 1 Low associées à l'univers de GTA 6 vont faire leur apparition le 19 novembre 2026. Un crossover particulièrement inattendu, qui réunira la licence la plus attendue de l'histoire du jeu vidéo, le géant américain du sportswear et l'un des artistes les plus influents de la scène hip-hop.
Si aucune annonce officielle n'a encore été publiée par les trois marques concernées, les premières informations disponibles dessinent déjà les contours de cette collection. Au programme : trois coloris, un prix annoncé de 130 dollars et une date de sortie qui coïncide parfaitement avec l'arrivée mondiale de GTA 6.
Trois coloris de Nike Air Force 1 annoncés, les premières images fuitent sur le net
D'après les informations relayées notamment par Sneaker News et Dexerto, cette collaboration prend pour base la célèbre Nike Air Force 1 Low '07. Trois déclinaisons sont associées à ce projet, chacune intégrant des accents Fire Pink :
Alors que le projet restait très mystérieux, un immense coup de théâtre a secoué les réseaux sociaux ce dimanche soir. Les toutes premières images réelles du coloris Black / Black / Fire Pink viennent de fuiter, dévoilant une paire en cuir noir premium texturé, truffée de détails cultes dédiés à l'univers de Vice City.
Le détail qui enflamme déjà la communauté est l'indice de recherche maximal à 6 étoiles, véritable signature historique de la franchise, gravé en rose fluo directement sous la semelle extérieure. De plus, une liasse de billets rose estampillée du logo officiel Grand Theft Auto entoure l'avant de la chaussure (toe box), imitant l'élastique qui retient les billets de banque lors des braquages. La paire sera livrée dans un packaging spécial avec des lacets noirs et des lacets interchangeables rose flashy.
Autre information majeure qui accompagne cette fuite : le prix de vente annoncé sera de 130 dollars par paire.
Un tarif qui place ces Air Force 1 dans une gamme relativement accessible pour une collaboration associant trois noms aussi importants que Nike, Travis Scott et Rockstar Games.
La commercialisation est prévue autour du lancement de GTA 6, avec une disponibilité potentielle auprès de certains distributeurs partenaires. Les modalités précises de vente, les quantités disponibles et les éventuelles conditions de distribution en Europe restent cependant à préciser. GTA 6 : comment le groupe Justice va révolutionner la musique du jeu
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 confie sa bande originale au duo français Justice. Une musique adaptative qui évoluera selon les actions de Jason et Lucia.
articles.txt:
Pour GTA VI, Rockstar ne mise pas uniquement sur un monde ouvert spectaculaire. Le studio confie également sa bande originale au duo français Justice, avec une partition capable d’évoluer en fonction des actions du joueur. Une approche musicale ambitieuse qui pourrait donner une autre dimension aux aventures de Jason et Lucia.
©Création IA Gemini Dans Grand Theft Auto, la musique a toujours occupé une place particulière. Les radios des véhicules, les morceaux cultes et les ambiances sonores participent pleinement à l’identité de chaque épisode. Pour GTA 6 (toujours attendu ce 19 novembre sur nos PS5 et Xbox Series) , Rockstar Games entend pousser cette dimension encore plus loin en faisant appel à Justice, le duo français composé de Gaspard Augé et Xavier de Rosnay.
Mais leur contribution ne se limitera pas à quelques morceaux destinés aux stations de radio de Vice City. Les deux musiciens signent une véritable bande originale, pensée pour accompagner l’expérience de jeu et s’adapter à la manière dont chacun explore l’univers de Leonida.
©Rockstar Games C’est sans doute l’aspect le plus intéressant de cette collaboration. Rockstar décrit le travail de Justice comme une « adaptive score », autrement dit une bande originale adaptative. Les compositions ont été conçues pour évoluer dynamiquement selon les situations rencontrées et la manière dont le joueur interagit avec le monde ouvert.
Concrètement, la musique doit pouvoir accompagner les différentes séquences de l’aventure, les déplacements et les moments de tension sans se limiter à une succession de morceaux fixes. L’objectif est de renforcer l’immersion dans les péripéties de Jason et Lucia, tout en donnant une identité sonore cohérente à cet immense terrain de jeu.
Pour Justice, cette liberté créative était essentielle. Le duo explique avoir dû explorer différentes émotions, textures et sonorités pour accompagner un univers aussi vaste, géographiquement que thématiquement.
Le choix de Justice n’a rien d’anodin. Récompensé aux Grammy Awards, le duo s’est imposé comme une référence de la musique électronique française, notamment grâce à son univers sonore immédiatement reconnaissable.
Un premier aperçu de ce travail est déjà disponible avec Flower in a Hurricane, morceau réalisé avec Tame Impala, SZA et King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Rockstar a également dévoilé Pusher, une nouvelle composition instrumentale sur laquelle Justice collabore avec un autre artiste français bien connu, Gesaffelstein.
La partition complète comptera 30 morceaux, auxquels s’ajouteront plusieurs pistes bonus numériques. Elle sera disponible le 11 décembre 2026 en divers formats.
Il ne faut toutefois pas confondre cette bande originale avec GTA VI: The Album. Ce second album rassemble 34 morceaux d’artistes variés et accompagnera le lancement du jeu, le 19 novembre.
D’un côté, les radios de Leonida permettront de retrouver une sélection musicale éclectique. De l’autre, Justice signera la musique originale qui accompagnera directement l’expérience de jeu.
En définitive, dans GTA 6, la musique ne sera pas seulement là pour meubler les trajets en voiture. Elle pourrait bien devenir l’un des ingrédients essentiels de l’immersion.

articles.txt:
When Rockstar Games released the record-shattering initial reveal trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI , it didn’t just showcase a return to a neon-soaked Vice City, it introduced the franchise’s first-ever dual-protagonist crime dynamic inspired by modern criminal history. At the heart of Leonida’s story are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval , a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde whose partnership will define both the narrative and the core gameplay mechanics of GTA 6 .
While GTA V pioneered the three-way character switching mechanic, GTA 6 takes the concept several steps further by building an interdependent relationship system where trust, survival, and combat synergy directly impact how your story unfolds.
Here is a deep dive into everything we know about Lucia and Jason, their character backgrounds, and how their dynamic will reshape open-world storytelling.
Lucia makes history as the franchise’s first playable female protagonist in the 3D/HD era. Opening sequences in official teasers depict her in an orange prison jumpsuit at the Leonida Penitentiary, conversing with a prison counselor about how “bad luck, I guess” landed her behind bars.
Story details suggest Lucia is sharp, resourceful, and driven by a desire for financial security and freedom at all costs. Her time in custody serves as a major plot catalyst, establishing a backstory rooted in high-stakes survival before she reunites with Jason to execute complex heists across Port Gellhorn and Vice City .
Where Lucia provides high-stakes ambition, Jason balances the duo with tactical precision and street-level pragmatism. Teased as a military veteran or former covert operator turned wheelman and enforcer, Jason’s background equips him with specialized weapon-handling skills, evasive driving tactics, and combat expertise.
Rather than operating as a classic solo mobster, Jason’s character trajectory is tied to his loyalty to Lucia, creating a tension between personal ambition, criminal risk, and partner devotion.
Rockstar North has overhauled the character-switching engine to work seamlessly during both free-roam and active missions:
One of the most ambitious narrative innovations in GTA 6 is the Relationship Trust System . Unlike static character traits, the bond between Lucia and Jason shifts dynamically based on player choices:
[ High Trust Level ] ──► Unlocks Syndicate Co-Op Combos & Higher Heist Cut Percentages ▲ │ Dynamic Player Choices & Shared Objectives ▼ [ Low Trust Level ] ──► Triggers Narrative Friction, Independent AI Actions & Altered Endings Mission Execution Style: Choosing non-lethal extractions or prioritizing your partner’s safety during ambushes increases mutual trust. Dialogue Choices: Casual interactions during long drives across the Leonida Keys feature branching dialogue options that build intimacy or foster distrust. Story Ramifications: Rumors indicate that relationship standing directly influences late-game narrative branches, determining whether the duo stays unified against law enforcement or split paths when the pressure escalates. 4. Modern Satire & The “Viral Fame” Dynamic Beyond their romantic and criminal bond, Lucia and Jason navigate a world obsessed with social media, livestreaming, and viral notoriety.
Throughout Vice City, local citizens and rival gang members film crimes on their smartphones in real time. Pulling off high-profile robberies as Lucia and Jason increases their in-game social media footprint—raising their reputation across Leonida’s underground networks while simultaneously alerting local news stations and law enforcement task forces to their physical appearances.
Lucia and Jason represent a major leap forward for Rockstar’s narrative storytelling. By combining modern romantic-crime tropes with interactive relationship mechanics, Grand Theft Auto VI promises to deliver one of the most compelling character dynamics in gaming history.

articles.t: GTA 6 dévoile six stations de radio : la curation musicale s'annonce exceptionnelle
articles.txt:
Les fans de Grand Theft Auto le savent bien : la bande-son est un élément central de l’expérience. Rockstar Games vient d’offrir un premier aperçu de six stations de radio qui seront disponibles dans GTA 6 , et le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que la curation musicale s’annonce une nouvelle fois exceptionnelle. Prévu pour le 19 novembre prochain, le jeu promet des heures d’écoute variées, entre tubes intemporels et découvertes plus pointues.
Rockstar a récemment mis en ligne des extraits audio de six stations, accompagnés de brèves descriptions. On y découvre une palette de genres très large, fidèle à l’esprit de la série. Voici les stations teasées :
Depuis Vice City , les stations de radio de GTA sont devenues cultes, reflétant à la fois l’époque et la culture du lieu. Avec GTA 6 , Rockstar semble vouloir perpétuer cette tradition en proposant un mélange éclectique qui couvre plusieurs décennies et styles. La présence de Flash FM , clin d’œil à la station emblématique de Vice City, ravira les fans de longue date. Mais ici, elle est modernisée avec des artistes contemporains comme Charli XCX et PinkPantheress, tout en conservant des titres plus anciens comme “Electric Feel” de MGMT (2007).
Le choix des animateurs est également intéressant : Alex Consani , mannequin et personnalité des réseaux sociaux, et Robyn , l’artiste suédoise connue pour son tube “Bulletproof”, officieront sur Flash FM. Ce duo inattendu promet des échanges savoureux, dans la plus pure tradition satirique de la série.
Autre nouveauté notable : GTA 6 sera le premier opus à proposer des podcasts en plus des stations musicales. Si Rockstar n’a pas encore détaillé le contenu de ces émissions, on peut s’attendre à des parodies hilarantes de la culture américaine, comme la série a su le faire par le passé avec des talk-shows ou des débats absurdes. Cette évolution renforce l’immersion dans l’État fictif de Leonida, inspiré de la Floride, et promet de longues heures d’écoute pour les joueurs qui aiment flâner en voiture.
La musique dans GTA n’est pas qu’un simple fond sonore : elle participe à l’identité du jeu et à l’immersion. Que ce soit en roulant de nuit sur les autoroutes de Leonida ou en explorant les quartiers animés, chaque station offrira une ambiance différente. Les amateurs de métal pourront headbanger sur Slayer, tandis que les fans de hip-hop sudiste retrouveront des classiques de la fin des années 90 et du début des années 2000. La diversité des genres est telle que chaque joueur devrait trouver son bonheur.
Rockstar n’a pas encore révélé le nombre total de stations, mais ces six premières annonces donnent déjà un aperçu alléchant. Avec une sortie prévue le 19 novembre 2025, les fans n’auront plus à attendre très longtemps avant de pouvoir composer leur propre bande-son criminelle.

articles.txt:
Le dernier « Grand Theft Auto » remonte à 2013. Et pourtant, Rockstar Games, l’éditeur de ce mastodonte des jeux vidéo, a réussi à faire patienter ses fans jusqu’à la sortie de « GTA 6 », le 19 novembre 2026, sans faire sombrer sa saga dans l’oubli.
Le problème, lorsque l’on a des fans, et qu’on désire leur offrir le plus grand jeu vidéo de leur vie, c’est que cela prend beaucoup de temps. Treize années se sont écoulées depuis la sortie du dernier jeu de la franchise « Grand Theft Auto », « GTA 5 » .
Le premier avantage qui a permis aux fans de pouvoir patienter pour jouer à « GTA 6 » , c’est que, derrière ces titres, il y a l’entreprise Rockstar Games. Cet éditeur ne fait pas exclusivement que du « GTA ». Le catalogue disponible sur leur site Internet évoque de nombreux autres jeux, bien qu’ils contiennent quasiment tous des armes et des véhicules.
C’est le cas de « Red Dead Redemption 2 », autre succès de Rockstar Games, qui a occupé la grande majorité des équipes de développement entre la sortie de « GTA », en 2013, et le début de la production de « GTA 6 », en 2018. On y incarne Arthur Morgan, un mercenaire, homme de main d’un chef de gang criminel, dans des États-Unis de la toute fin du XIXe siècle.
On y retrouve l’ADN de « GTA », avec des hors-la-loi qui évoluent dans un univers cruel, un monde ouvert et vivant, un joueur libre et une narration très forte.
Ce jeu n’est pas qu’un en-cas exclusivement bon à patienter. Lui aussi, comme son grand frère, « GTA 5 », squatte les classements. Si ce dernier est le deuxième jeu vidéo le plus vendu de tous les temps, derrière « Minecraft », avec plus de 230 millions de ventes, la troisième place revient à « Red Dead Redemption 2 » et ses presque 90 millions d’exemplaires vendus.
Même le « Mario Kart » le plus vendu de toute la saga le talonne seulement, avec 80 millions de ventes environ.
Mais il y a un autre jeu qui a permis à la licence « GTA » de survivre en attendant son nouvel opus. Une déclinaison de « GTA 5 », sortie juste après ce titre : « GTA Online ».
Dans cette version multijoueur et en ligne du mastodonte, les joueuses et joueurs sont invités à créer un personnage à partir de zéro et à fonder un empire criminel. Révolution : « GTA » devient quasiment infini.
Au départ, le jeu est capricieux. Il ne fonctionne pas tout à fait correctement, et présente de nombreux problèmes de performances et de réseau. Mais au fil des années, il est amélioré, mis à jour, et continue d’être approvisionné en contenu très régulièrement, y compris en 2026.
Si Rockstar Games maintient ce jeu un peu particulier en vie, c’est parce qu’ils inscrivent « GTA » dans la logique moderne de l’industrie du jeu vidéo en en faisant un « jeu service ». C’est une logique économique qui consiste à faire d’un jeu une « plateforme » régulièrement mise à jour et dans laquelle les joueuses et joueurs injectent de l’argent en continu, plutôt que de livrer un produit qui ne sera acheté qu’une seule fois.
Il n’existe pas de chiffres transparents et officiels, mais les différentes analyses estiment que « GTA 5 » a généré 10 milliards de dollars. La moitié provenant simplement des ventes du dernier opus, l’autre moitié venant de « GTA Online », dont les joueuses et joueurs utilisent de l’argent réel pour acheter de l’argent virtuel utilisable en ligne.
Il reste un dernier atout qui a empêché la saga de sombrer dans l’oubli à force de patienter pour le prochain opus. Il s’agit du « RP », pour « roleplay », qui signifie jeu de rôle.
Des joueuses et joueurs se réunissent sur des serveurs en ligne de « GTA Online », et se mettent dans la peau de personnages dont ils adoptent la personnalité, l’histoire, et les objectifs. C’est une sorte de théâtre d’improvisation, extrêmement populaire sur les réseaux sociaux.
En définitive, difficile de s’ennuyer si on est fan de « GTA », qui propose pléthore de solutions pour continuer à profiter de ce qui la rend si populaire.

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Grand Theft Auto's radio stations have long stood as an integral part of the series' whole vibe—either offering time capsules of the times each game was set in (Vice City), or offering a realistic blend of classic and modernity a la Grand Theft Auto 5 's excellent music curation.
Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.
I've been just a tad giddy to discover what awaits me in Grand Theft Auto 6 's car stereos when the game launches on November 19, which has me surprised that Rockstar teasing six of its upcoming stations earlier this month completely flew under my radar.
Well, now I've had a gander and listened to all 12 minutes of its DJs bantering and a peppering of bangers between. And I gotta say, I'm already jazzed to speed down Leonida's highways with some of these stations at full volume.
Rockstar's licensed music curation rarely misses, and that very much seems to be the continuing trend with Grand Theft Auto 6. While we don't know just how many radio stations there are in total yet—this is the first game where we'll be able to tune in to both terrestrial music stations and podcasts, it being 2026 and all—but the six that were teased were the exact kind of flavours I've come to expect from the series.
There's Latin station Cocoteo FM, classic country Back Country Radio, African channel AfroBANK FM, all-out metal hub The Chamber 106.6, pop banger central Flash FM, and hip-hop destination Dirty South Classics. I'm already 100% here for The Chamber's setlist, being an elder emo and all, with bands like Black Sabbath, Pantera, and Slayer making their way onto Leonida's airwaves. But I'm also jazzed to see newer blood on the scene, like Bad Bunny's appearance on Cocoteo.
My biggest interest was in Flash FM, though. Non-Stop Pop has become such an iconic radio station for me, thanks to some excellent song choices and Cara Delevigne's delightfully deadpan delivery. It doesn't seem like I'm going to be disappointed, though—Alex Consani takes up the mantle as model-turned-radio-host alongside the excellent artist Robyn (of Bulletproof fame), and hearing one of my favourite songs in MGMT's Electric Feel is all the confidence I need in Rockstar's keen ear.
While the previews do show criminally little interactions between the hosts (it seems like Grand Theft Auto 6 is going for duos across all its stations, presumably for some easy back-and-forth banter), I'm sure there'll still be satire in droves to come.

articles.t: GTA 6 lead channels the spirit of Skyrim-era Todd Howard:
articles.chapeau: Rockstar
articles.txt:
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter While Rockstar has teased the size of GTA 6's playable map a few times, the heads behind the next Grand Theft Auto outing also want you to know that it's not all hollow space. Anywhere you go, there's intentionality.
Speaking to Edge , Rockstar says GTA 6's map is nearly as large as the combined efforts of Grand Theft Auto 4, 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2. But it doesn't stop there. While you often see procedural generation to achieve sheer size, Rockstar leans on a human touch to ensure the map is dense with interest. Rockstar North co-studio lead Aaron Garbut says GTA 6 features "an order of magnitude more interiors" than what's come before.
"Every back alley is as densely detailed and interesting as the others," he says. "You can go anywhere, any random location, and so many people have thought about that location."
Such is the case; Garbut says he's still finding new things despite having explored the game for many years during its development.
Rockstar's ambition is the sort we've seen in the games industry for many years, as developers drum up excitement by teasing scale and interactivity we've never seen before. When marketing Skyrim , Bethesda boss Todd Howard famously said "that mountain is not just a backdrop; you can walk all the way to the top of that mountain."
He isn't the only one, of course – Randy Pitchford did something similar with Borderlands 4 just last year. Still, the sense that there's something more to what's in front of you than what's come before is something I still enjoy. It speaks to an ambition to reach a new level in a way I find almost nostalgic.
And there's plenty of that with GTA 6. Edge mentions that the homes of strangers you come across aren't merely blank. There's history on the walls, in the form of photographs, alongside the sort of clutter in living rooms and kitchens that gives off the vibe that someone lives here, making an entry into a house feel like trespassing.
Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more
On that, Garbut shares a story about walking into a home and finding pictures of the family pet, only to walk into the next room and find that very dog, and the consequences its owner is going to face for leaving them alone.
"The whole place was trashed," he says. "There was shit in the corner, smeared around a bit."
"You can have your life in the game": GTA 6 promises to be an RPG like nothing the series has ever seen, but Rockstar says there's still a balance to strike.

articles.t: GTA 6 Lets You “Have Your Life in the Game,” Says Rockstar
articles.chapeau: However, co-studio head Rob Nelson doesn't want to "feel like you're foisting things on the player and then have them reject those things."
articles.txt:
While it lacks a leveling system, loot tiers and other tropes you would typically associate with a role-playing game, Grand Theft Auto 6 is certainly closer to the genre than previous titles. The sheer choice in role-playing Lucia, Jason or both, whether building bonds, going to the gym (and keeping a steady sleep schedule), or the consequences of your actions, is overwhelming.
“You can really make the game what you want it to be at the time, whether that’s more of a roleplay experience where you’re buying cigarettes and beer in the shop and going on the train for the day, or going to a club,” said head of development Aaron Garbutt to Edge Magazine (via GamesRadar ). “You can have your life in the game.”
With Rockstar aiming to make this the most realistic GTA game yet, it can be a lot to handle. You can’t even carjack anything as easily as previous games or escape the police’s attention by simply avoiding them for extended periods. Even cars must be refuelled . Co-studio head Rob Nelson noted how, “You don’t want to feel like you’re foisting things on the player and then have them reject those things. It’s more about trying to let people lean into the way they want to play.”
That sounds a lot like what senior VP of narrative Rupert Humphries said last month about realism for the sake of immersion and foregoing that for “what’s convenient for the player.” But for those who vibe with that balance, there are a lot of options. For example, head of technology Phil Hooker talked about the bus systems and how he’s “memorized all of the routes,” because he likes taking public transport instead of driving.

Le mois de novembre 2026 s'annonce particulièrement intéressant pour les joueurs sur PC, PS5, Xbox Series et Nintendo Switch 2. Entre l'arrivée très attendue de GTA 6 le 19 novembre , le retour de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, plusieurs jeux indépendants et de nouvelles versions de titres populaires, il y aura de quoi s'occuper. Voici notre calendrier des principales sorties jeux vidéo de novembre 2026, avec les dates et les plateformes pour ne manquer aucun lancement.
Le mois sera notamment marqué par l'arrivée de Grand Theft Auto VI , mais plusieurs autres jeux méritent également leur place dans votre agenda. Les amateurs de RPG, de simulation, de jeux d'action ou d'aventures indépendantes auront différentes nouveautés à découvrir.
Retrouvez ci-dessous notre sélection des sorties de novembre , classées chronologiquement.
Les dates correspondent aux informations annoncées à ce jour et peuvent évoluer selon les éditeurs. Certaines entrées concernent des portages, des éditions améliorées ou des extensions, et non de nouveaux jeux à proprement parler.
Difficile de parler des sorties de novembre sans évoquer GTA 6 , qui occupe une place particulière dans le calendrier de cette fin d'année.
Après une longue attente, Rockstar Games prévoit de lancer Grand Theft Auto VI le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X|S . Pour le moment, aucune date de sortie PC n'a été officiellement annoncée.
Cette nouvelle aventure nous emmènera dans l'État fictif de Leonida, avec une version moderne de Vice City et ses environs. Les joueurs suivront notamment Jason et Lucia, deux personnages entraînés dans une histoire criminelle qui promet de les conduire bien au-delà d'un simple braquage.
La sortie de GTA 6 pourrait naturellement concentrer une bonne partie de l'attention des joueurs durant la seconde moitié du mois. D'autres productions tenteront toutefois de se faire une place avant ce rendez-vous.
Les possesseurs de Nintendo Switch 2 seront particulièrement bien servis en novembre, avec plusieurs titres déjà connus qui feront leur arrivée sur la console.
Le 5 novembre , Nintendo accueillera une nouvelle version de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , avec des graphismes retravaillés, une bande-son réorchestrée et une modernisation du gameplay.
La même journée marquera l'arrivée de Stellar Blade Complete Edition , comprenant les contenus additionnels déjà publiés ainsi que de nouvelles tenues. Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition rejoindra également le catalogue de la console.
Une semaine plus tard, le 12 novembre , les amateurs de RPG pourront découvrir Metaphor: ReFantazio, tandis que Pikmin 4 reviendra dans une édition Nintendo Switch 2 accompagnée de l'Académie Dandori.
Enfin, SONIC PICO PARK proposera de nouvelles épreuves multijoueurs, et The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ rejoindra la console le 19 novembre, avec notamment la coopération en ligne.
Le mois ne se résumera évidemment pas à GTA 6 et à Nintendo. Dès le 3 novembre , les joueurs PC pourront découvrir l'accès anticipé de Loftia, un jeu de simulation de vie multijoueur à l'ambiance cosy. Les amateurs de RPG narratifs retrouveront également ZERO PARADES dans sa version Director's Cut sur consoles.
Le 4 novembre, Lightyear Frontier passera en version 1.0 sur PC et Xbox Series. Le lendemain, à minuit en France, Blizzard lancera World of Warcraft: Forever, une nouvelle expérience permanente permettant de redécouvrir Azeroth.
Autre date à retenir, le 10 novembre , avec trois sorties très différentes. Football Manager 27 reviendra pour les passionnés de gestion footballistique, Shrek 2 Remastered proposera de retrouver l'aventure de 2004 en version modernisée, tandis que Warhammer Survivors misera sur des affrontements contre des hordes d'ennemis.
Si novembre 2026 sera surtout associé à GTA 6, ce calendrier montre que les joueurs auront bien d'autres occasions de découvrir de nouveaux univers ou de retrouver des aventures déjà appréciées.

articles.t: GTA VI : à l'approche de la sortie du jeu, les arnaques se multiplient | TF1 Info
articles.chapeau: [VIDÉO] Le très attendu jeu vidéo GTA VI sortira le 19 novembre sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series.  Des chercheurs en cybersécurité ont repéré des centaines de sites qui exploitent l'impatience des joueurs pour leur soutirer de l'argent ou des données.  Ces pièges circulent depuis le mois de juin et pourraient se multiplier d'ici la sortie, selon les spécialistes. - GTA VI : à l'approche de la sortie du jeu, les arnaques se multiplient (Nouvelles technologies).
articles.txt:
Le dernier volet de la série Grand Theft Auto (GTA), des jeux d'action où le joueur incarne des criminels, est sorti en 2013 et s'est écoulé à près de 230 millions d'exemplaires, selon son éditeur. Sa suite , qui sort dans moins de trois semaines, est très attendue : la première bande-annonce de GTA VI a été vue plus de 90 millions de fois sur YouTube en 24 heures, un record. Cet engouement attire les escrocs, qui misent sur la popularité du jeu pour piéger ses fans.
En septembre, des chercheurs de l'entreprise de cybersécurité Avast ont recensé en une seule journée plus de 200 noms de domaine liés à GTA, dont 10% classés à risque moyen ou élevé, a rapporté (nouvelle fenêtre) franceinfo. Parmi eux, certains imitent le PlayStation Store, la boutique en ligne de Sony, pour vendre une "édition Ultime" du jeu. Le piège paraît d'autant plus crédible que cette version existe réellement, au prix de 99,99 euros, relève (nouvelle fenêtre) Clubic.
Pour suivre l'usage des données saisies, les chercheurs ont payé avec des cartes "canary", sans argent, qui signalent toute tentative de débit. D'autres sites misent sur les cryptomonnaies, vantant un jeton virtuel inspiré du jeu. Luis Corrons, expert en cybersécurité chez Avast, s'attend à une accélération : "Il y a de fortes chances que nous observions beaucoup plus d'arnaques au cours de la semaine qui précède la sortie de GTA VI" , a-t-il déclaré à franceinfo.
Ces pièges circulent pourtant depuis plusieurs mois. Le 23 juin, deux jours avant l'ouverture des précommandes, l'entreprise de cybersécurité Malwarebytes a signalé (nouvelle fenêtre) des sites vendant un "accès anticipé VIP" au jeu pour plusieurs centaines de dollars en cryptomonnaie. "Vous payez, vous n'obtenez rien, et comme le paiement se fait en cryptomonnaie, il n'y a généralement aucun moyen de récupérer votre argent" , a expliqué son chercheur Stefan Dasic.
En juillet, l'éditeur d'antivirus Kaspersky a repéré (nouvelle fenêtre) de faux sites de précommande copiant le PlayStation Store, avec de faux avis cinq étoiles. En août, Malwarebytes a identifié (nouvelle fenêtre) des pages se faisant passer pour Rockstar, le studio qui développe le jeu, et proposant une démo qui n'existe pas : le fichier téléchargé contenait un logiciel conçu pour voler des mots de passe. Début septembre, l'entreprise a décrit (nouvelle fenêtre) un faux site vendant une copie "fuitée" du jeu pour 50 dollars (environ 43 euros), qui cherchait en réalité à vider le portefeuille de cryptomonnaies de ses visiteurs.
"Une augmentation entre 9 et 17%" : aux États-Unis, la sortie imminente du jeu vidéo GTA VI fait grimper les demandes de congés
Aux États-Unis, où l'action du jeu se déroule dans une ville inspirée de Miami, la chaîne locale CBS Miami a relayé ces mises en garde le 18 octobre. Chris Mawson, fondateur du site d'actualité Power Up Gaming, y explique que les escrocs jouent sur "la peur de passer à côté" et conseille de ne jamais cliquer sur un lien promettant un téléchargement anticipé. Le jeu ne sortira que sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series : toute offre pour ordinateur ou smartphone est une arnaque.

articles.chapeau: Carte géante, météo plus crédible, police bien plus futée, véhicules à gérer: Rockstar Games pousse GTA 6 vers un réalisme nettement plus lourd.
articles.txt:
Carte géante, météo plus crédible, police bien plus futée, véhicules à gérer: Rockstar Games pousse GTA 6 vers un réalisme nettement plus lourd.
Le plus frappant, ce n’est pas la taille de GTA 6 . C’est le prix à payer pour faire n’importe quoi. D’après les mécaniques montrées chez Rockstar Games , le fantasme du chaos gratuit prend un coup, avec une police plus agressive, des PNJ qui observent tout et des véhicules qu’on ne balance plus comme des mouchoirs.
Leonida , avec Vice City et ses régions autour, serait environ deux fois plus grande que la carte de GTA 5 . L’ensemble du territoire serait même comparable à la somme des maps jouables de GTA IV , GTA V et Red Dead Redemption 2 . Oui, ça commence à causer.
Mais le vrai saut est ailleurs. Rockstar Games promet beaucoup plus d’intérieurs, un cycle jour-nuit plus long, des routes plus étroites et surtout une météo bien plus fine, influencée par le vent, l’humidité, le brouillard, l’heure et la saison. Les orages se voient arriver au loin, touchent l’environnement, perturbent les véhicules, et poussent même les passants à se mettre à l’abri. Ajoutez à ça environ 600 000 animations pour varier les comportements, des traits de personnalité assignés aux PNJ et des quartiers aux profils démographiques distincts. Bref, le décor ne veut plus juste faire joli.
Le duo Jason et Lucia pourra être alterné seulement quand le récit le permet. Pendant certaines courses-poursuites, on pourra changer de personnage , y compris pour laisser l’IA conduire pendant qu’on gère la riposte.
Leur relation sera suivie sur une échelle à quatre niveaux. Elle progresse en passant du temps ensemble, balade sur la plage, vélo, salle de sport si l’abonnement a été acheté, ou simple virée en voiture. Et il y a une vraie couche de vie quotidienne, acheter des cigarettes, une bière, sortir en club. Des consommables donneront aussi des bonus, café pour l’endurance, shake protéiné pour la santé.
Porter une arme à la main ou dans le dos ne passera plus inaperçu. Les PNJ réagiront, pourront paniquer, vous défier, voire intervenir pendant un braquage. Même logique pour les témoins, les scènes de crime et la police, qui ne poursuivra plus juste un point sur la carte.
Le système de recherche suivra des éléments précis, tenue portée, armes visibles, action en duo, images de vidéosurveillance. Des icônes à l’écran indiqueront ce que les forces de l’ordre savent. Du coup, fuir pourra vouloir dire changer de fringues, jeter ses armes ou se séparer de son partenaire. Et la réponse montera vite, radios coordonnées, barrages, herses, hélicoptères, chiens. Pas mal de chaos, mais plus vraiment sans conséquence.
Cette fois, une caisse a une jauge de carburant et un indicateur d’état moteur. Son état comptera aussi à la revente chez un receleur. Les armes pourront être stockées dans le coffre, ce qui rend le véhicule central dans la préparation d’un coup.
Certaines voitures récentes pourront même diffuser leur position après un vol, pendant que leur propriétaire signale le larcin. On pourra se faire livrer un véhicule via une appli, chercher des modèles demandés via WAINK , ou tomber sur des PNJ qui provoquent en course sauvage. Clairement, dans GTA 6 , voler une voiture sera enfin plus intéressant que juste appuyer sur accélérer.

GTA 6 Leak 13: Beach Gameplay and Prologue Spoilers [2026]
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 Leak 13 showed Vice City beach gameplay on Aug. 25. See how the Cyberleek story unfolded and what to expect in the final 18 days.
articles.txt:
Nadia Dubois November 1, 2026 12 min read The 13th GTA 6 leak put a crowded Vice City beach on screen on August 25, 2026. Protagonist Jason rides a bike across the sand, stops near clusters of NPCs, and the camera shows crowds stretching toward the horizon. GameRant and RockstarINTEL both covered the clip the day it surfaced, and Forbes described the run of daily clips as hitting a full week.
Today is November 1, and GTA 6 is 18 days from its November 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A lot has changed since Leak 13. Our earlier Cyberleek explainer tracks the full run of clips, and this article goes deeper on the beach leak, the prologue poll that followed it, and where the story stands now.
One correction up front. The beach clip and the prologue poll are not breaking news this morning. They date to late August. What makes them worth revisiting is how the campaign escalated afterward, and how little of it has been confirmed by Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive. This is a news analysis of that arc, with every number tied to a named outlet.

Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
According to GameRant, which published its write-up on August 25, the clip is gameplay footage of Jason riding a bike along a Vice City beach. He stops occasionally to look at groups of NPCs. The outlet noted that you can hear the NPCs holding conversations as Jason passes, that some stand in small clusters, and that a few of them hold cellphones in a way that reads as realistic.
RockstarINTEL titled its coverage around the same point: the leak shows an incredible number of NPCs. Fan accounts put the visible crowd at somewhere between a hundred and two hundred figures across the sand and in the water. That count is an eyeball estimate, not a Rockstar spec, so treat it as a rough scale rather than a technical claim. Umbrellas and other beach structures fill the background.
The choice of scene matters. Crowd density is one of the hardest things for an open-world game to fake, because every extra pedestrian costs animation, audio, and AI budget. A beach at sunset is close to a stress test. Our look at the reported 600,000 NPC animations covers the engineering side of why that crowd behavior is a big deal.
Cyberleek did not pick the scene alone. GameRant reported that the leaker had run an earlier poll asking followers to choose between a nudist town, a strip club, and a beach. The nudist town won the vote, yet fans argued that the beach would show off NPC density better. The beach clip landed as Leak 13.
That detail tells you something about the strategy. The leaks were not a one-off data dump. They worked as a serialized release, with audience votes steering each drop. Polls keep followers engaged, give every clip a built-in news hook, and let the leaker claim that fans, not the leaker, chose what to publish.
The pattern also made each leak easy to cover. Outlets such as GameRant, Kotaku, and Forbes could report the next poll, then the clip that followed, then the reaction. A daily cadence with a vote attached produces a news cycle on demand. Whether that counts as protest or promotion is a question we return to in the memecoin section below.
The headline threat attached to Leak 13 was the next poll. GameRant reported that Cyberleek was asking followers whether to leak the prologue featuring Lucia, and that the vote was leaning toward yes when the beach story ran. Fans speculated that the leaker had access to a restricted build containing only the prologue. That theory is a fan inference, not a confirmed fact.
Kotaku reported on August 26 that the leaker had begun sharing story spoilers. The footage appeared to be the game’s opening prologue, with Lucia in prison, the same setting as the official 2023 debut trailer. Kotaku said she wears an orange jumpsuit and that additional backstory details were revealed. The poll that looked like a threat on August 25 had become a leak by the next day.
Gameplay clips show mechanics. Story clips show plot. Spoilers hit harder, because a player cannot unsee an opening sequence, and Rockstar builds its marketing around narrative reveals. Kotaku said the leaker included a message claiming the build is recent and that the game is not ready. That is Cyberleek’s claim. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has verified it, and the reported release date has not moved.

articles.t: GTA 6 Expectations: 18 Days to Nov 19 Launch [2026]
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 launches Nov 19, 2026, just 18 days away. See what fans expect from Vice City, the story, graphics and gameplay, and which dreams may fall short.
articles.txt:
Sofia Lindström November 1, 2026 13 min read Rockstar Games has a fan problem that no day-one patch can fix. SVG argued on October 31, 2026 that GTA 6 players have each built a private version of the game in their heads, and that those versions contradict one another. Writer Joe Roberts points to a split between fans who want deeper realism and fans who want the old, unrestricted chaos. eTeknix carried the same story as the countdown to the November 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S entered its final 18 days.
The stakes are large. Circana’s PlayerPulse research puts purchase intent at 29% among U.S. console and PC gamers, the highest reading the firm has recorded for any game, as we covered in our look at what the 29% number leaves out . Intent that high means millions of people hold a mental blueprint of what they are about to buy. Every one of those blueprints differs a little, and Rockstar can only ship one game.
This analysis separates what SVG and other outlets reported from what remains open. It covers the expectation gap, the confirmed launch facts, the money riding on the date, and five predictions for how the gap plays out after release. Anything Rockstar has not confirmed is labeled that way.
· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
The SVG piece, dated October 31, 2026, builds its case from a simple observation. Fans do not want the same things from GTA 6, and many of the things they want cannot coexist in one game. The article walks through several examples that show the collision.
One camp wants mandatory systems such as car refueling, because they read the series’ move toward simulation as a promise of consequences. Another camp wants the opposite and argues that games should work as an escape, not a second job. A third group hopes for a deep, emotionally grounded story with fully drawn characters, a tone far from the satire the franchise built its name on. Others expect to walk into most buildings on the map, which the article treats as unlikely.
SVG uses Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 4 and the original 1997 Grand Theft Auto as reference points. The logic runs like this. Rockstar has spent years signaling that GTA 6 takes the detail of its last big release further. That pitch invites the realism crowd to expect friction and depth. It also frightens the crowd that remembers the series as a playground where a rampage costs nothing.
The piece does not claim Rockstar has misstepped. Its argument is that the studio faces a structural trap. Satisfying one expectation set weakens the other, and silence from Rockstar lets each fan fill the gaps with whatever they prefer.
Open-world games rarely fail on a single feature. They fail when a feature set fights its own design goals. Mandatory refueling is a clean example. For one player it adds texture to a long drive through Leonida. For another it turns a getaway into a chore at the worst possible moment.
Rockstar has handled this tension before by layering systems. Red Dead Redemption 2 let players ignore many survival mechanics and still finish the story. The open question for GTA 6 is whether the same layering can cover a wider spread of desires than any previous entry faced. The fan base is also far larger and more online than it was in 2013.
Every long wait produces imagination. Rockstar released its first GTA 6 trailer in December 2023 and its second in May 2025, according to TechRadar’s coverage of the records. That left fans with two short films, scattered screenshots and years of speculation. Gaps in information get filled, and people fill them with their own taste.
This group reads every polished frame as evidence of simulation depth. They expect believable police response, weather that matters, and characters who feel like people. When they say they want a deeper story, they mean one that treats Jason and Lucia as more than vehicles for set pieces.
This group wants the physics sandbox. They bought earlier entries to launch cars off ramps, trigger wanted levels and see what the systems allow. To them, each added layer of realism is a tax on the fun. SVG notes that this view runs through the series’ history and still has plenty of defenders.

articles.chapeau: Rockstar reportedly sent a free GTA 6 poster to a fan who emailed. What eTeknix, Dexerto and Games.gg confirm, and what stays unverified.
articles.txt:
Nadia Dubois November 1, 2026 12 min read Rockstar Games is reportedly sending free GTA 6 posters to fans who email the company, according to an eTeknix report that follows an October wave of Reddit posts. The trigger was a fan in São Paulo, Brazil, who bought the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition with his first paycheck, wrote to Rockstar asking for a signed poster, and received an official one by DHL from the company’s New York office. Other Reddit users say the same approach worked for them.
The story is small, but it lands at a loaded moment. GTA 6 launches on Nov. 19, 2026, and our rundown of what is confirmed about the Nov. 19 launch and its $79.99 price shows how tightly Rockstar controls what reaches the public. A personal gesture from an executive stands out against that backdrop. This analysis sorts what the coverage actually establishes from what remains a claim, and what the episode says about marketing, fan relations and the weeks ahead.
· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
The eTeknix piece carries a deliberately cautious headline: Rockstar is reportedly sending free posters. The word reportedly matters. The underlying account comes from one Reddit user, identified in Games.gg coverage as aogustoo, who described his email as a long shot. He told the community he had bought the Ultimate Edition with the first paycheck from a new job and wanted a signed poster for his bedroom wall.
Dexerto and Games.gg both published their versions on Oct. 10, 2026, and the tale spread from there. According to Dexerto’s account, a Rockstar executive answered by saying the company would be happy to send a poster once posters were produced, and added that he could not sign it because he was an executive, not the creator. The poster later arrived in Brazil in a DHL parcel, and the shipping label pointed to Rockstar’s office in New York.
eTeknix says the poster shows the main GTA 6 key art, with protagonists Jason and Lucia in the foreground. The fan planned an unboxing video and blurred the executive’s name and email address before posting the exchange. That redaction is a small detail with a big consequence: readers cannot independently check who replied.
The mechanics, as relayed by the outlets, are simple. A fan writes to Rockstar, explains why they care about the game, and asks for a poster. No form, no contest, no code. Games.gg describes the fan’s email as a shot-in-the-dark message, and eTeknix summarizes the process as requiring nothing more than an email to the company.
What the reports do not give you is just as important. Nobody has published an official address for poster requests. Rockstar has not said how many posters exist, who qualifies, or whether international shipping is routine. The Brazil delivery shows the company will ship abroad in at least one case, but one parcel is not a policy.
The fan himself urged the community not to flood Rockstar with copycat requests. He called the gesture a rare act of kindness from someone on the team, which is the opposite of a promise that every email gets an answer. Anyone planning to write in should read that caution first.
Separating the layers of this story keeps the headline honest. Some elements appear in several outlets and come from the fan’s own screenshots. Others rest on anonymous commenters. The table below lists each claim, who carries it, and how much weight it can bear today.
The pattern is familiar. A single named account gets amplified, and a looser claim (anyone can do this) rides along with it. The reported part of the story is credible enough to cover. The giveaway part is not established.
Dexerto notes that some commenters questioned whether the exchange was real. That skepticism is reasonable and costs nothing to hold. A screenshot of an email with the sender blurred proves little by itself. A DHL label from New York is harder to fake casually, yet it still comes from the same person making the claim.
Compare this with other GTA 6 rumors the site has tracked. In our look at the reviewer trap rumor, which rested on one insider and zero proof , the claim spread because it was exciting, not because anyone could check it. The poster story is far lower stakes and far more plausible. Sending a poster costs a few dollars, harms nobody, and fits a company that wants goodwill before a huge launch.

articles.chapeau: Persona 1 remake trailer leaked online Oct. 31: 360p footage, Unreal Engine debug text, no word from Atlus or Sega. What is reported and what is not.
articles.txt:
Marcus Chen November 1, 2026 12 min read Gameplay footage that appears to show a remake of the original Persona surfaced online on October 31, and by that evening GameRant, TheGamer, PushSquare, Gematsu and several other outlets were covering it. The Persona 1 remake leak is unconfirmed. Neither Atlus nor its parent Sega has said the project exists, and nobody has verified when or by whom the clip was recorded.
The clip first drew attention on Reddit, where a user named Dastanovich posted it to the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit under the title Persona: Be Your True Mind remake gameplay leak, according to TheGamer. The file reportedly began life on the file-hosting site gofile, uploaded by an unknown account. The same Persona 1 remake trailer footage then moved across social media within hours, which is how most console-era leaks travel once a forum thread catches fire.
Timing makes the story hard to ignore. Atlus is about 3.5 months from launching a Persona remake that is already announced, and our earlier report on the Persona 4 Revival Shadow trailer covered the February 18, 2027 release date for that game. A second, older Persona title showing up in leaked form while the first one is still in its marketing window gives fans plenty to argue about. This article lays out what was reported, what each outlet could and could not verify, and what the leak would mean for Atlus if the footage turns out to be real.
· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
Early reports describe a video of just under two minutes that shows three kinds of scenes: field exploration, battle, and event scenes built around 2D illustrations. articles.chapeau: GTA 6 may skip review watermarks, but Tom Henderson cites 'insane security measures.' Rockstar confirmed none. What is known, reported and unknown.
articles.txt:
Sofia Lindström October 31, 2026 13 min read Rockstar Games may not be stamping a flashing name on Grand Theft Auto VI review copies, but the studio is reportedly running other tight controls around the game. Notebookcheck’s coverage of the story centers on one line from Tom Henderson, who said Rockstar has “some insane security measures in place, though.” Rockstar has not confirmed any of it.
The claim that started this round of chatter was simple. Review builds, the story went, show a flashing reviewer name so a leak can be traced back to whoever received the copy. Insiders pushed back fast, and we walked through that dispute earlier in our piece on GTA 6 review copies, watermarks and leakers . What remains is a narrower and more interesting question: if the watermark is wrong, what is Rockstar actually doing?
The honest answer today is that nobody outside the company has published details. This article sorts the claims by how well they hold up, explains what “security measures” usually means for a pre-release game, and lays out what the reported November dates would imply for reviewers and readers. Every specific claim below is attributed to the outlet or person who made it, and anything the reporting leaves unconfirmed is labeled that way.

Start with the short list of things that are solid. Rockstar Games has not publicly confirmed the alleged watermarking system, and it has not confirmed the reported blacklist policy for reviewers or outlets that leak footage. That is the only fully firm statement in this story, and it is a statement about silence.
Everything else sits in a band between “reported” and “disputed.” The watermark claim was challenged by insiders, including NateTheHate and Tom Henderson. The nature of the security measures Henderson alluded to has not been disclosed. The review embargo date and the launch date both appear in coverage, but neither has been confirmed by the publisher in the cited reporting.
Read the table from the bottom up and you can see how the story is built. The dates and the blacklist are reported but unconfirmed. The watermark is the most specific claim and the most heavily contested. The security-measures line is the vaguest, which is exactly why it carries the least risk of being proven wrong and the least information.
A visible, flashing reviewer name is a very specific design choice. It would be easy to spot, easy to describe, and easy to screenshot. That specificity cuts both ways. If it existed, reviewers who had seen it would likely confirm it, and the people who dispute it would have a hard time being so flat about it.
Two named figures did dispute it. NateTheHate said that to his knowledge the claim is not accurate. Tom Henderson went a step further in framing, saying he found no evidence supporting the watermark claim. Neither statement proves a negative. They do, however, move the claim from “plausible rumor” toward “probably wrong.”
We saw a similar pattern with an earlier rumor that review copies might contain a booby trap for leakers. That one rested on a single source and no proof, as we laid out in the GTA VI reviewer trap rumor breakdown . The watermark claim follows the same arc. A dramatic mechanism gets attached to a game that everyone is watching, and the lack of a public denial from the publisher gets read as quiet confirmation.
From a production standpoint, a flashing name across footage is a blunt tool. It is distracting for the reviewer, it spoils capture for any legitimate coverage, and it invites tampering. A leaker can crop, mask or re-record around an overlay. Studios that care about traceability tend to prefer marks that are hard to see and hard to strip. That is general industry logic, not a statement about Rockstar, but it explains why insiders found the flashing-name story hard to believe.

It concedes the watermark point and then redirects, signaling that the absence of one specific trick does not mean the absence of protection.

articles.chapeau: Rockstar's 12 new GTA 6 screenshots show rural Leonida, the Grassrivers swamp and a hammerhead shark, three weeks before the Nov. 19 launch.
articles.txt:
Nadia Dubois October 31, 2026 11 min read Rockstar Games handed Edge magazine 12 new GTA 6 screenshots on October 29, and the batch spends as much time outside Vice City as inside it, according to Notebookcheck. One image shows a motorcycle gang riding through a small rural town. Another puts armed men on an airboat in the Grassrivers swamp. A third drops the camera under the surface for a hammerhead shark. With launch set for November 19, 2026, these GTA 6 screenshots are the clearest look yet at how much of Leonida lives beyond the neon.
The images came packaged with a 16-page Edge cover feature built on a visit to Rockstar North in Edinburgh. Rob Nelson of Rockstar told the magazine the game is “ready,” Game Rant and The Daily Scrum News both reported. If you want the full list of dates, prices and platforms Rockstar has actually confirmed, our GTA 6 launch tracker for Nov. 19 at $79.99 keeps that sorted from the rumors.
This analysis covers what the 12 images show, what the accompanying interview adds, why the timing matters three weeks before release, and where the open questions remain. Every detail below is attributed to the outlet that reported it. Anything Rockstar has not confirmed is labeled as such.
